figures.caption: The published multi-scale workflow: a global crack analysis identifies critical regions, refined thermal simulations drive local grain growth, and microstructural descriptors feed back into the failure model.
figures.original_caption: Approach for the numerical prediction of cracking as a function of the microstructure; z is the building direction.
figures.alt: Four-stage workflow from macro-scale crack-critical regions through meso-scale thermal fields and micro-scale grain simulation to a microstructure-dependent cracking model.
figures.scope_note: Wider research pipeline in the 2026 paper, not a claim that every stage is provided by this repository or solely authored by Ferdinand Schnell.
figures.transformations: Rasterized with Poppler and cropped; original figure content, colors, labels, and annotations retained. Original typeset caption omitted from image and recorded here.

figures.caption: As-built microstructures in the later study: measured EBSD maps and pole figures for PP0 and PP2 above, simulated grain maps below. Grain morphology improved, while the predicted crystallographic texture remained imperfect.
figures.original_caption: Microstructure characterization in the as-built state: (a) EBSD image (PP0), (b) pole figures (PP0), (c) EBSD image (PP2), (d) pole figures (PP2), (e) simulated EBSD image (PP0), (f) simulated EBSD image (PP2); z is the building direction.
figures.alt: Measured colored EBSD maps and circular pole figures for PP0 and PP2, with two simulated colored grain maps below; scale bars are 100 micrometres.
figures.scope_note: The 2026 paper's model and results; not a fresh run of the thesis code or the repository's small example.
figures.transformations: Rasterized with Poppler and cropped; original figure content, colors, labels, and annotations retained. Original typeset caption omitted from image and recorded here.

figures.caption: Measured and simulated grain characteristics across PP0-PP3. The later model captured increasing grain size and aspect ratio, with reported maximum deviations of 20% and 16%; it did not reproduce the experimental Schmid-factor trend.
figures.original_caption: Comparison of the experimentally and simulatively determined grain characteristics: (a) grain sizes and aspect ratios, (b) Schmid factors.
figures.alt: Two charts compare experiment and simulation across process parameter sets PP0 to PP3: grain size and aspect ratio on the left, Schmid factor on the right.
figures.scope_note: The 16% aspect-ratio deviation here is a different quantity from the paper's approximately 16% reduction in mean crack length.
figures.transformations: Rasterized with Poppler and cropped; original figure content, colors, labels, and annotations retained. Original typeset caption omitted from image and recorded here.

figures.caption: Experimentally measured crack lengths for four process parameter sets. The paper reports an approximately 16% shorter mean crack length in the representative PP3-versus-PP0 crack-shape comparison discussed with Fig. 15 on the same page; this is a collaborative experimental result.
figures.original_caption: Experimentally identified crack lengths with changing process parameters.
figures.alt: Box plots of mean crack length in millimetres for PP0, PP1, PP2, and PP3; red crosses and a dashed line mark the means.
figures.scope_note: Experimental process-parameter comparison in the 2026 paper. The 16% statement is reported in the discussion of Fig. 15(b), PP3 (350 W, no hatch rotation), compared with PP0 (285 W, rotating hatch); it is not a percentage calculated from this crop, a normalized simulated crack length, or a performance claim for this repository's standalone example.
figures.transformations: Rasterized with Poppler and cropped; original figure content, colors, labels, and annotations retained. Original typeset caption omitted from image and recorded here.

figures.caption: A 2024 thesis verification case: with bulk nucleation disabled (N0 = 0), a single melt track solidifies by growth from existing grains at the melt-pool boundary.
figures.original_caption: Single melt track with nucleation N0 = 0, where all growth stems from existing grains along the melt pool boundary.
figures.alt: A long, narrow, colored single melt-track cross section shows grains growing from an existing melt-pool boundary; a color scale shows grain orientation angle.
figures.scope_note: A controlled verification result, not evidence that the thesis model reproduced realistic multi-layer microstructure.
figures.transformations: Rasterized with Poppler and cropped; original figure content, colors, labels, and annotations retained. Original typeset caption omitted from image and recorded here.

figures.caption: A revealing thesis result: grains can cross the yellow build-layer boundaries, but irregular nucleation prevents realistic columnar growth and consistent grain-size trends. The circles mark contrasting local grain structures in a 285 W case.
figures.original_caption: Grain structure in the X-Z plane cut in the middle, with the powder bed height at each layer marked in yellow. Output of Simulation Scenario 2 with 285 W laser power.
figures.alt: Colored grain structure in an X-Z cross section with horizontal yellow layer boundaries and three circles highlighting differently sized and oriented grains.
figures.scope_note: Read with thesis printed pages 45-47 and 49-51: this is evidence of both implemented multi-layer growth and the model's validation limitations.
